question: The integration of AI Mode and AI Overviews into Google Search raises concerns about minors’ exposure to generative AI through a service routinely used for education. Where these functionalities cannot be disabled independently of traditional search, schools and guardians may lack effective control over children’s exposure, even when standalone AI chatbots are blocked.
The Digital Services Act (DSA) requires very large online search engines to assess and mitigate systemic risks, including risks to minors and mental well-being. 1.

Has the Commission verified whether Google adequately assessed these risks before deploying or expanding these functionalities in the EU, and will it use Article 67 DSA to obtain the relevant assessments and information on safeguards for educational accounts?

Will the Commission assess whether compliance with Article 35 DSA requires allowing schools and guardians to disable generative AI independently while retaining traditional search, including through interim measures under Article 70 where the legal conditions are met?

How is the Commission assessing whether the underlying Gemini models fall within, and comply with, the EU AI Act’s obligations for general-purpose AI models with systemic risk, particularly regarding risks to minors?
